mainInsight: Walk the list once and flip each node's next pointer to point at its predecessor, keeping the next node in a temporary variable before overwriting the pointer.

approaches.name: Recursive reversal
approaches.summary: Reverse the rest, then attach the head at the end.

approaches.name: Iterative three pointers
approaches.summary: prev, curr, next: flip curr.next = prev and advance.

promptVariants: Which variables does iterative reversal use?
What is the loop's core step?
options: prev, curr and a saved next pointer
A stack of values pushed and popped in order
Two heaps holding the first and second halves
A hash map from each node to its next pointer
cards.answer: prev, curr and a saved next pointer
cards.explanation: Save curr.next, point curr to prev, then advance both.

promptVariants: What is true about prev and curr at the start of each iteration?
cards.answer: prev is the head of the already-reversed prefix (initially None) and curr is the first node of the not-yet-reversed suffix. After flipping curr.next to prev, curr becomes the new head of the reversed part.
cards.explanation: At the end prev is the new head.

promptVariants: Extra space of the iterative version: ___
Complete the statement: Extra space of the iterative version: ___
Why must `nextt = curr.next` be saved before `curr.next = prev`?
What does the function return when the loop ends?
cards.code:
while curr:
    nextt = curr.next
    curr.next = prev
    prev = curr
    curr = nextt
return prev
cards.answer: Overwriting curr.next would lose the rest of the list; the temporary keeps the way forward. When the loop ends curr is None and prev is the last original node, which is the head of the reversed list.
cards.explanation: The original head's next becomes None automatically.

promptVariants: What does the function return for an empty list?
How does a single node behave?
options: None for an empty list; a single node is returned unchanged
An error, since there is no head node to reverse
A new empty node that has no value or next pointer
The node pointing to itself as a one-node cycle
cards.answer: None for an empty list; a single node is returned unchanged
cards.explanation: The loop is skipped for empty input and runs once for one node (its next becomes None).

incorrectOptionExplanations.The node pointing to itself as a one-nod: Its next is set to prev = None.
